title: Lattice Composer
pages: Separate a solar prism in the t7 Prism Separator for a Prism Core. Laminate one Sealed Steel Plate in the t8 Lattice Laminator for a Laminated Lattice. Hand two more Prism Cores to an Astral Font holding 320 lumen to make a Core Halo. Craft the Lattice Composer with the halo in the bottom-left slot, a separate Prism Core, the Laminated Lattice, a Collimated Lens, one sealed steel plate, two glass panes, a crafting table and a separator. This hand-performed rite gates t7 to t8; no machine makes the halo.

Feed the base material into the left slot and its binder into the adjacent slot. Both are consumed. Each recipe uses 24 FE/t for 160 ticks. The output slot holds the combined component. Prism core and amethyst shard form phase lattice for the next tier.

Metal fittings give spare rare ingots a use. Any forge:ingots tag member works. Recipes: 3 titanium + chest = hopper; 4 zirconium + furnace = blast furnace; 2 thallium + attuned quartz = daylight detector; 1 ruthenium + redstone torch = 2 repeaters; 1 rhenium + blaze powder = 4 fire charges; 2 rhodium + comparator = observer; 2 palladium + stone pressure plate = 6 detector rails. Feed them by hopper or pipe to make automation parts in bulk.

More t8 workshop fittings: 2 gallium + redstone = 2 pistons; 2 germanium + string = 4 tripwire hooks; 2 hafnium + redstone = dispenser; 2 indium + shroomlight = 2 end rods; 4 osmium + chipped or damaged anvil = anvil (osmium reforges a worn anvil). These spend metal to supply automation, lighting and repair stations; none creates a tier component, and recycling a fitting never returns more iron or redstone than its binder held plus one per rare ingot spent.

Other metal paths serve the workshop: 2 nickel + hay block = 2 target blocks for redstone hit detection; 2 silver + glowstone dust = soul lantern for safe blue lighting; 3 tungsten + blaze powder = brewing stand; lead + string = a weighted fishing rod; tin + honeycomb = 2 candles; zinc + gunpowder = 3 firework rockets without paper; 2 aluminum + paper = name tag; 2 platinum + compass = lodestone (the needle anchors in the metal). Each ingot enters through its forge:ingots tag, and none of these returns more string, paper or gunpowder than it took when recycled.

Further metal fittings: 3 antimony + gold block = bell (antimony-hardened bell metal for village alarms); 2 bismuth + clay ball = decorated pot; 2 chromium + bow = crossbow; cobalt + blue terracotta = blue glazed terracotta, which slime and honey blocks cannot pull; 2 iridium + flint = flint and steel. These spend gold, clay, a bow, blue terracotta or flint, and recycling never returns more of that binder. Datapack recipes assemble functional components and phase lattice. JEI shows both inputs, output, time and FE. Type arcana_industry:composition accepts ingredient, binder, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Highest priority wins, then recipe ID.

Final workshop fittings: 2 manganese + iron bars = 2 heavy weighted pressure plates for rail controls; 2 molybdenum + iron ingot = shield for expedition defense; 2 niobium + piston = sticky piston for movable machinery; 3 tantalum + ender pearl = ender chest for remote storage; 2 vanadium + gold ingot = 3 powered rails for longer transport lines. All five take forge:ingots tags. Recycling these outputs cannot return more of their consumed binder; powered rails return at most one gold ingot from three rails.

Additional utility stations consume tagged ingots: 2 antimony + stone = stonecutter for precise shaping; 2 bismuth + paper = cartography table for map work; 2 chromium + furnace = smoker for faster cooking. Each binder is consumed, and each recipe takes 160 ticks at 24 FE/t. Feed two ingots into the base slot and the binder into its adjacent slot.

Trait rule: a composed part may only carry material traits that its feed and binder bring in. The pool is the base input times its count plus the one binder, so 2 prismarine shards and a glowstone block can make a sea lantern (luminous 4) but shards with glowstone dust cannot. Glass alone has crystalline 1, which is why the daylight detector needs attuned quartz and the spyglass needs an amethyst shard. If a datapack recipe adds a trait its inputs lack, the composer shows Product traits not in input or field, keeps its inputs and spends no FE.

Top and horizontal ports import into either input; the bottom exports the output. Buttons configure each face. FE capability and manual crank power the machine. It pauses on a full output or when its status reads Product traits not in input or field; inventory, FE, work progress and side modes persist. Breaking drops all slots.
